source.quote: Shanling's own announcement for the EC Zero T MAX, read 2026-11-25; the product page /product/499 is 14 image slices, and the download page /download/152 labelled « EC Zero T Max » serves the EC Zero T's file, /download/files/ECZeroT.pdf - there is no MAX-specific manual. Verbatim: « MAX comes with the same R2R module as the original EC Zero T, featuring 24-bit architecture with 192 high-precision 0.1% resistors. »; « The upgraded amplifier circuit was designed around AD8397, delivering increased output without any need for external power and achieving significantly reduced output impedance. »; « Thanks to the upgraded amplifier circuit, EC Zero T MAX provides up to 1300mW @ 32Ohm Balanced / 361mW @ 32Ohm Single-Ended output power while running directly on its battery »; « Available at 629 USD / 689 Eur ». NO PCM rate, no DSD figure and no input bit depth appears anywhere.

facts.chip: « the same R2R module as the original EC Zero T, featuring 24-bit architecture with 192 high-precision 0.1% resistors » - a discrete ladder, 24 bits deep, no part number. The amplifier is « designed around AD8397 », which is what the MAX changes.

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_ni_DoP_ni_natif_ne_sont_dits_pour_ce_mo: DoP appears on no Shanling page or manual, and « native » only in the UA dongle manuals and in EM5. Neither is stated for this model, so both fields are absent rather than guessed.
_le_24_bits_est_larchitecture_de_lECHELL: « 24-bit architecture with 192 high-precision 0.1% resistors ». That 24 describes the ladder, and the sentence says so. `bits` is NOT written: on the EC Zero T, whose module this is, the input accepts 32 bits while the ladder is 24 - so copying this 24 into `bits` would halve the device's stated input depth using a number about its output stage. Fifth record today where a maker publishes a ladder depth beside an input depth, and the first where only the ladder's is given.
_ce_quon_ne_PEUT_PAS_heriter_du_modele_d: The maker says the converter module is identical to the EC Zero T's, and the EC Zero T's page states « USB DAC Supports: 768kHz/32bit, DSD512 ». It would be one line's work to carry those figures across. They are NOT carried: « the same R2R module » is a statement about the module, not about the USB receiver, the firmware or the filter menu, and the announcement explicitly changes the amplifier circuit. The download page even serves the base model's manual, which is an invitation to conflate them. A record with no rate is the honest outcome of a page with no rate.
